global.h3: Russian barrage kills 17 in Kyiv as interceptors run low
global.summary: Overnight missile and drone strikes on Kyiv killed at least 17 people and wounded 44, with Zelensky warning that allied interceptor shortages cost lives.
body: Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight killed at least 17 people and wounded 44 others, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, as emergency crews worked through what officials called a massive attack. Warehouse facilities in Brovary were among the sites hit and a separate fire broke out at a warehouse in Bucha.

Zelensky said lives could have been saved had allies replenished Ukraine's stock of missile interceptors, renewing his appeal for air defence supplies as Russia sustains a high tempo of long-range strikes into a fourth summer of the war.

global.h3: Ukrainian drones strike Wildberries warehouse near Moscow
global.summary: Kyiv answered the Kyiv barrage by hitting Russian crossings, warehouses and military targets, including a large Wildberries logistics hub south of Moscow.
body: Ukraine said its forces struck Russian river crossings, warehouses and other military targets in response to the overnight assault on Kyiv. A Ukrainian drone hit a Wildberries warehouse south of Moscow, the retailer and the regional governor confirmed.

The deep-strike exchanges cap a record July in which Russia fired a wartime monthly high of missiles at Ukraine, with both sides increasingly targeting logistics and energy infrastructure far behind the front.

global.h3: Russian advance slows to 13 square miles in four weeks
global.summary: OSINT tracking shows Russia's summer offensive stalling, gaining far less ground than in the prior month despite heavy bombardment.
body: Russian forces made a net gain of about 13 square miles of Ukrainian territory in the four weeks to August 4, according to the DeepState OSINT group, down sharply from 31 square miles in the preceding four-week window.
Analysts say Moscow's spring-summer push has failed to translate intense missile and drone activity into meaningful territorial gains, even as civilian casualties from rear-area strikes climb.

global.h3: Kuwait says it intercepted Iranian drones over its airspace
global.summary: The Kuwaiti defence ministry reported detecting and downing Iranian drones as the Gulf stays on edge over the Hormuz standoff.
body: Kuwait's defence ministry said its military detected and intercepted Iranian drones entering the country's airspace, a sign of how the Strait of Hormuz crisis is spilling into the wider Gulf.
The incident came as tankers reported strikes near Oman and shipping through the strait fell to a trickle, keeping regional militaries on heightened alert.

global.h3: Iran and Oman agree new Hormuz shipping lanes
global.summary: Tehran said it settled coordinates for new commercial routes through the strait with Oman, but warned the deal does not end the crisis.
body: Iran announced it had agreed with Oman on the coordinates of new commercial shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz after several rounds of talks, a partial step toward reopening the vital chokepoint.

A senior Iranian military adviser stressed Tehran would allow shipments only along its stipulated route and warned that US warships transiting other paths would be targeted, leaving the arrangement fragile.

global.h3: Trump signals Hormuz reopening could come within days
global.summary: Washington voiced optimism that a deal to reopen the strait was near, with European help offered to clear mines from the waterway.
body: President Donald Trump said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could come as early as midweek, with Iran discussing terms directly with Oman and signalling it would let certain European countries help clear mines from the strait.
Iran cautioned that any agreement would not fully resolve the crisis, underscoring the gap between diplomatic momentum and conditions on the water.

global.h3: Brent slides about 7% on Hormuz de-escalation hopes
global.summary: Oil fell hard as traders priced in a possible reopening of the strait, with Brent settling near $84 and WTI near $80.
body: Brent crude settled down about $6.35 at $83.77 a barrel, a fall of roughly 7%, while WTI dropped $4.33 to $80.34 as markets bet on an easing of the Hormuz standoff.

Shipping analysts said only a handful of vessels were transiting the strait each day, and detours around Africa were adding at least two weeks to affected voyages, keeping freight and insurance costs elevated even as crude prices retreated.

global.h3: Trump's Section 301 tariffs hit more than 60 countries
global.summary: New levies of 10% to 12.5% now cover dozens of trading partners, with China and Vietnam at the higher band.
body: The administration imposed Section 301 tariffs on more than 60 countries in late July, setting rates of either 10% or 12.5% with numerous exemptions. China and Vietnam face the 12.5% band, while Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia sit at 10%.
Analysts at the Tax Foundation estimate the 2026 tariffs amount to an average tax increase of about $900 per US household and have not meaningfully narrowed the trade deficit.

global.h3: Some US firms quietly reshore back to China despite tariffs
global.summary: Reporting finds the levies pushing companies back toward Chinese suppliers rather than boosting domestic manufacturing.
body: Trump's tariffs were meant to revive American manufacturing, but reporting indicates some US companies that had shifted away from China are now reinvesting in Chinese suppliers as the shifting duty regime makes alternatives costlier and less reliable.
The pattern complicates the stated goal of reshoring, with firms citing supply-chain depth and price advantages that tariffs alone have not offset.

global.h3: Washington and Beijing signal trade truce before deadline
global.summary: China indicated progress toward a trade understanding with the US ahead of an August tariff deadline.
body: Beijing signalled it was moving toward a trade truce with Washington ahead of an August deadline, easing some fears of a fresh escalation in the tariff war between the world's two largest economies.
Details remained thin, and observers cautioned that prior signals have not always translated into durable agreements.

global.summary: Record heat has fuelled deadly blazes across southern Europe, with Spain suffering its worst wildfire deaths in two decades.
body: Fires across Europe had killed at least 17 civilians, six firefighters and two helicopter crew by August 4 and forced roughly 330,000 people from their homes in Spain and France alone, making it the deadliest wildfire season in Spain in about 20 years.

Blazes have scorched Spain, Portugal, France, Greece, Italy and Turkey. Greece remains hardest hit, with a fire west of Athens entering its sixth day and around 14,400 hectares burned across Attica and Boeotia.

global.h3: Copernicus: Western Europe just logged its hottest June
global.summary: The record heat behind the fire season pushed French temperatures to their highest since national records began.
body: June 2026 was the hottest June on record for Western Europe, averaging 20.7C, about 3.05C above the 1991-2020 norm, the Copernicus Climate Change Service said. Anomalies peaked near +9C over France and Germany, and the mercury reached 45.1C at Andujar in southern Spain.
France recorded its hottest day since national records began in 1947, part of a broader pattern of intensifying summer heat straining health systems, agriculture and power grids.

global.h3: Low Danube threatens Hungary's only nuclear plant
global.summary: Drought-shrunken rivers are disrupting European power and shipping, pushing Hungary's Paks plant toward a forced slowdown.
body: The Danube's historically low levels are disrupting nuclear power operations, with Hungary coming close to a forced shutdown of its only nuclear plant as cooling water runs short. Low water on the Rhine is also hampering barge traffic and energy supplies.
The strains highlight how the same heat driving Europe's wildfires is squeezing the continent's rivers, energy and logistics at once.

global.h3: China-Japan friction over Taiwan grinds on
global.summary: Beijing keeps up economic and diplomatic pressure on Tokyo as cross-strait tensions simmer.
body: China has sustained a pressure campaign against Japan since Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi suggested in late 2025 that a Taiwan contingency would likely implicate Japan, keeping East Asian relations tense through the summer.

Taiwan, meanwhile, continues to emphasise deterrence amid Chinese maritime pressure and delays in US arms deliveries, with its coast guard periodically expelling Chinese vessels from restricted waters.

netherlands.h3: Limburg wildfire rages as drought grips the country
netherlands.summary: A stubborn wildfire in Limburg has stretched firefighters amid record dryness, with safety regions warning the country can handle only one big blaze at a time.
body: A large wildfire continued to burn in Limburg as the Netherlands endures one of its driest summers on record. Safety regions warned that the country's firefighting capacity cannot cope with more than one major blaze simultaneously, raising the stakes as heat and drought persist.
The precipitation deficit is approaching the 1976 record, leaving heathland and forest tinder-dry and prompting repeated warnings against open flames.

netherlands.h3: Deadly day at the coast: swimmer and two rescuers drown
netherlands.summary: A missing swimmer was found dead at Callantsoog and two women drowned trying to save a child, a grim day on Dutch beaches.
body: A swimmer who went missing at Callantsoog was found dead, and separately two women drowned while trying to help a child in the water, authorities reported. The incidents added to a difficult stretch for coastal safety during the hot spell.
Lifeguards have repeatedly warned about strong currents and crowded beaches as the heatwave draws large numbers to the sea.

netherlands.h3: Jetten and Halsema warn of rising anti-LGBTQ+ hatred
netherlands.summary: The prime minister and Amsterdam's mayor cautioned about growing hostility toward LGBTQ+ people as WorldPride wound down in the capital.
body: Prime Minister Rob Jetten and Amsterdam mayor Femke Halsema warned of rising anti-LGBTQ+ hatred, speaking as WorldPride events coloured the capital. Both urged vigilance against intolerance even amid the celebrations.
The comments come as the minority Jetten cabinet, sworn in on February 23, navigates a polarised social climate alongside its economic agenda.

netherlands.h3: Fifth terror-plot arrest in a single week
netherlands.summary: Dutch police detained another young man on suspicion of preparing an attack, the fifth such arrest in a week.
body: Another young man was arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist attack, the fifth such arrest in the Netherlands within a week, authorities said. The cluster of cases has drawn attention to the radicalisation of young suspects.
Officials have not detailed a common thread but say the pace of arrests reflects heightened monitoring of online activity.

netherlands.h3: Almere alderman accused of abusing 14 children
netherlands.summary: An Almere alderman faces accusations of sexually abusing 14 children, a case that has shaken local politics.
body: An alderman in Almere was accused of sexually abusing 14 children, prosecutors indicated, in a case that has stunned the municipality and prompted questions about oversight.
The allegations are among the most serious to hit a serving Dutch local official in recent memory and are expected to dominate council discussions.

netherlands.h3: EU AI Act's second stage forces AI-content labelling
netherlands.summary: From August 2, companies distributing mainly AI-generated content in the Netherlands must label it as such under the AI Act.
body: The second stage of the European Union's AI Act came into force on August 2, requiring companies in the Netherlands that distribute content primarily created with AI to label it clearly. The rules aim to improve transparency for consumers.
The step is part of a phased rollout that will progressively tighten obligations on AI developers and deployers across the bloc.

netherlands.h3: House prices keep climbing as supply lags
netherlands.summary: Dutch home prices continue to rise, though DNB expects the pace to cool to 3-4% a year through 2028.
body: Dutch house prices have kept rising, with recent quarters showing strong year-on-year gains, but De Nederlandsche Bank projects annual growth of 3% to 4% between 2026 and 2028, notably slower than the previous year.
Falling consumer confidence and higher mortgage rates are curbing borrowing capacity, even as supply remains tight, according to DNB and lender forecasts.

netherlands.h3: Inflation near 2.7% as growth stays subdued
netherlands.summary: DNB sees 2026 inflation around 2.7% while the IMF pencils in modest 1.2% growth for the Dutch economy.
body: DNB projects Dutch inflation of about 2.7% in 2026, lower than in 2025 but nudged up by energy costs, while the European Commission's forecast runs a touch higher at 3.2%. The IMF expects growth of 1.2% this year, rising to 1.4% in 2027.
The projections assume implementation of the Jetten coalition agreement, though officials caution that a minority government makes full delivery less certain.

netherlands.h3: Government approves 2026 rent increases of at least 4.1%
netherlands.summary: Dutch tenants face regulated rent rises of at least 4.1% this year under a government decision.
body: The Dutch government approved rent increases of at least 4.1% for 2026, adding to cost-of-living pressure for renters already squeezed by a tight housing market.
The decision feeds into the broader affordability debate that continues to shape Dutch housing politics.

netherlands.summary: Amsterdam hosted a festive close to WorldPride, drawing crowds despite warnings about intolerance.
body: WorldPride brought a festive atmosphere to Amsterdam, with events across the city drawing large crowds even as officials warned about rising anti-LGBTQ+ hostility.
The celebrations offered a counterpoint to a tense summer marked by heat, drought and a run of security incidents.

mood.p: Nederland beleeft een broeierige, kurkdroge zomer met veel zon en oplopende temperaturen. Het neerslagtekort blijft hoog, rivieren staan laag en de brandweer waarschuwt voor natuurbranden na de hardnekkige brand in Limburg. In Amsterdam hangt tegelijk een uitgelaten stemming door de nasleep van WorldPride, terwijl het land zich langzaam opmaakt voor het einde van de vakantie.
